review_candidates.title: Hardware Engineer — Founding Team
review_candidates.description: About Clira Health Clira Health is building an at-home blood monitoring platform for high-risk hematology patients, founded by a repeat founder and an AP-HP transplant nephrologist tackling a hard problem with broad clinical impact. Patients with acute leukemia or undergoing stem-cell transplantation often need several blood tests each week for immune system monitoring. We are developing a fully automated system that painlessly collects and analyzes a blood microsample at home, starting with CBC + CRP . Our long-term goal is to move beyond static blood measurements toward high-frequency biomarker monitoring, enabling care teams to intervene earlier and, ultimately, anticipate complications before they become critical. We are an early-stage, venture-backed medtech company based in Paris, with offices and laboratory space inside Saint-Joseph Hospital. We build our technology in-house, from blood collection to analysis. The role We work by feature, not by discipline. You will own features of our device end to end, and you are responsible for getting them into production. Nobody takes over after the prototype. If you built it, you ship it. Owning a feature means: Designing it: the mechanism, the electronics, the firmware and the software it needs Building it: making and assembling your own prototypes in our in-house workshop (FDM and SLA printing, laser cutting, metal CNC) Proving it works: requirements, test rigs, verification, reliability Making it compliant: risk analysis, design documentation and standards testing for your feature, with the support of our senior regulatory consultant Making it manufacturable: design for manufacturing and test, suppliers, production fixtures, first builds Mechanics is the largest part of the work, and the electronics, firmware and software come with it: Mechanics: mechanisms, miniature actuation, material selection, sealing, tolerances and fits, in CAD and on the bench Motion and control: microliter metering, sample handling, microscope autofocus Boards: motor drives with magnetic encoders, pumps, valves and pressure sensing, heaters, optical sensors, battery power, flex circuits Firmware: closed-loop motion, sequencing, communication Software: test automation, data acquisition and analysis, mostly in Python We expect you to understand the problem, challenge assumptions and own the result. Who we are looking for We care more about what you can build than your degree or credentials. You may be a great fit if you have built complex physical systems across mechanics, electronics and software, and enjoy difficult technical problems. You build them to serve a great product, and you care about the person who will use it. We value: A bias toward building and testing fast High agency and intensity Extremely high standards for product quality Obsession with understanding why things work or fail A willingness to challenge existing solutions The belief that “impossible” only becomes impossible once you have proved it No specific school, degree or certification is required. Show us what you have built. Compensation We work hard and expect a lot, but we pay accordingly. Competitive salary: 50-90k Meaningful equity package Standard French startup benefits: Meal vouchers, Navigo reimbursement, etc. Apply Email hiring@clirahealth.com Tell us: Why you want to join Clira What you have accomplished or built in the past Links, photos, videos, GitHub, CAD, side projects and failed experiments are very welcome.

How The Work Is Approached The work begins with listening closely to a request and identifying the issue that actually needs attention. A useful reply explains the next step in accessible language, while an accurate case note makes the interaction understandable to anyone continuing it. When a matter falls outside established procedures, the right response is to escalate it instead of improvising an unsupported answer. Core Responsibilities Handle customer inquiries across approved support channels. Troubleshoot routine issues and document outcomes. Maintain accurate case notes and follow-up status. Escalate unresolved or sensitive cases appropriately. Contribution and outcomes Good support makes everyday interactions easier to navigate. Organized records reduce repeated explanations, careful follow-up helps unresolved requests move forward, and a steady tone keeps conversations constructive even when customers are frustrated. Remote collaboration and quality Because colleagues may rely on shared systems rather than in-person conversations, organized notes are important. Explain what has been completed, what remains unresolved and which next action is needed. Treat sensitive records with appropriate discretion and follow established procedures when an issue requires another person's judgment. The role particularly values patient communication, sound recordkeeping and dependable follow-through. Relevant Capabilities Clear written and verbal communication Basic customer service and ticketing software Patience, accuracy, and confidentiality What Dependable Performance Looks Like The goal is straightforward: complete assigned work with care, make outcomes understandable and leave the next person with reliable information. Thoughtful communication also makes handoffs easier to understand and helps prevent unnecessary repetition. Careful habits, professional communication and consistent follow-up create value beyond any single completed task.
